breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह अधिनियम में सबसे व्यापक, सबसे लचीली धारणा धारा है -- प्रभावी रूप से सामान्य तर्कसंगत अनुमानित तर्क ('अनुभव के सूत्रों') का संहिताकरण। यह रोकी गई साक्ष्य से प्रतिकूल अनुमान (उदाहरण (छ)) और हाल/अस्पष्टीकृत कब्जे (उदाहरण (क)) के बारे में तर्कों के लिए एक पसंदीदा आधार है, लेकिन उपधारा (2) की मामला-विशिष्ट सावधानियाँ भी उतनी ही महत्वपूर्ण हैं और अक्सर अनदेखी कर दी जाती हैं।

sections.title: Presumption as to absence of consent in certain prosecution for rape
sections.raw_text:
120. In a prosecution for rape under sub-section (2) of section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the question is whether it was without the consent of the woman alleged to have been raped and such woman states in her evidence before the Court that she did not consent, the Court shall presume that she did not consent.
Explanation.—In this section, "sexual intercourse" shall mean any of the acts mentioned in section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

breakdown.plain_summary: In an aggravated-rape prosecution under BNS section 64(2), once sexual intercourse by the accused is proved, and the complainant testifies before the Court that she did not consent, the Court must presume absence of consent -- shifting the practical burden onto the accused to establish consent.
essential_elements: Applies specifically to prosecutions under BNS section 64(2) (aggravated categories of rape).
Preconditions: sexual intercourse by the accused is proved, and the woman states in evidence that she did not consent.
Mandatory presumption ("shall presume") of absence of consent once those preconditions are met.
Explanation ties "sexual intercourse" to the acts defined in BNS section 63.
breakdown.how_to_read: This closes Chapter VII with a mandatory presumption significant to sexual offence trials -- it operates alongside section 149's proviso (barring character/past-sexual-history questions on the consent issue) to protect complainants once intercourse is proved and non-consent is testified to.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: बीएनएस धारा 64(2) के अंतर्गत गंभीरीकृत-बलात्संग अभियोजन में, एक बार जब अभियुक्त द्वारा यौन संभोग सिद्ध हो जाए, और परिवादिनी न्यायालय के समक्ष गवाही दे कि उसने सहमति नहीं दी थी, तो न्यायालय को सहमति के अभाव का अनुमान लगाना होगा -- जिससे व्यावहारिक भार सहमति सिद्ध करने के लिए अभियुक्त पर स्थानांतरित हो जाता है।
essential_elements_hi: विशेष रूप से बीएनएस धारा 64(2) (बलात्संग की गंभीरीकृत श्रेणियों) के अंतर्गत अभियोजनों पर लागू होता है।
पूर्वशर्तें: अभियुक्त द्वारा यौन संभोग सिद्ध हो, और स्त्री साक्ष्य में यह कहे कि उसने सहमति नहीं दी थी।
उन पूर्वशर्तों के पूरा होने पर सहमति के अभाव की अनिवार्य धारणा ('मानेगा')।
स्पष्टीकरण 'यौन संभोग' को बीएनएस धारा 63 में परिभाषित कृत्यों से जोड़ता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह अध्याय VII को यौन अपराध विचारणों के लिए महत्वपूर्ण एक अनिवार्य धारणा के साथ बंद करती है -- यह धारा 149 के परंतुक (सहमति के मुद्दे पर चरित्र/पूर्व-यौन-इतिहास प्रश्नों को रोकना) के साथ मिलकर कार्य करती है ताकि एक बार संभोग सिद्ध हो जाने और असहमति की गवाही दिए जाने पर परिवादिनियों की रक्षा की जा सके।

sections.title: Estoppel
sections.raw_text:
121. When one person has, by his declaration, act or omission, intentionally caused or permitted another person to believe a thing to be true and to act upon such belief, neither he nor his representative shall be allowed, in any suit or proceeding between himself and such person or his representative, to deny the truth of that thing.
Illustration.
A intentionally and falsely leads B to believe that certain land belongs to A, and thereby induces B to buy and pay for it. The land afterwards becomes the property of A, and A seeks to set aside the sale on the ground that, at the time of the sale, he had no title. He must not be allowed to prove his want of title.

breakdown.plain_summary: Opens Chapter VIII with the general definition of estoppel: if someone intentionally, by declaration/act/omission, causes or permits another to believe something and act on that belief, that person (and their representative) cannot later, in litigation between them, deny the truth of what they represented.
essential_elements: Requires: a declaration, act, or omission by one person.
That conduct must intentionally cause or permit another person to believe a thing to be true.
The other person must actually act upon that belief.
Effect: neither the representor nor their representative may deny the truth of that thing in a suit/proceeding between them.
breakdown.how_to_read: Estoppel is a rule of evidence, not a source of substantive rights -- it stops a party from asserting a fact contrary to their earlier representation, but doesn't itself create title or liability (as the Illustration shows: A is estopped from denying he had title, but the estoppel operates only between A and B).
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अध्याय VIII को विबंध (एस्टॉपल) की सामान्य परिभाषा के साथ खोलती है: यदि कोई व्यक्ति जानबूझकर, घोषणा/कृत्य/लोप द्वारा, किसी और को कुछ मानने का कारण बनाता है या अनुमति देता है और उस विश्वास पर कार्य कराता है, तो वह व्यक्ति (और उसका प्रतिनिधि) बाद में, उनके बीच के वाद-विवाद में, उसने जो प्रदर्शित किया उसकी सत्यता से इनकार नहीं कर सकता।
essential_elements_hi: आवश्यकता है: एक व्यक्ति द्वारा घोषणा, कृत्य, या लोप।
वह आचरण जानबूझकर किसी अन्य व्यक्ति को किसी बात को सत्य मानने का कारण बनाए या अनुमति दे।
अन्य व्यक्ति को वास्तव में उस विश्वास पर कार्य करना चाहिए।
प्रभाव: न तो प्रदर्शनकर्ता और न ही उसका प्रतिनिधि उनके बीच वाद/कार्यवाही में उस बात की सत्यता से इनकार कर सकता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: विबंध साक्ष्य का एक नियम है, मूल अधिकारों का स्रोत नहीं -- यह किसी पक्ष को उसके पहले के प्रदर्शन के विपरीत तथ्य का दावा करने से रोकता है, लेकिन स्वयं कोई हक या दायित्व उत्पन्न नहीं करता (जैसा उदाहरण दिखाता है: A अपना हक होने से इनकार करने से विबंधित है, लेकिन विबंध केवल A और B के बीच कार्य करता है)।

sections.title: Estoppel of tenant and of licensee of person in possession
sections.raw_text: 122. No tenant of immovable property, or person claiming through such tenant, shall, during the continuance of the tenancy or any time thereafter, be permitted to deny that the landlord of such tenant had, at the beginning of the tenancy, a title to such immovable property; and no person who came upon any immovable property by the licence of the person in possession thereof shall be permitted to deny that such person had a title to such possession at the time when such licence was given.

breakdown.plain_summary: A specific application of estoppel to landlord-tenant and licensor-licensee relationships: a tenant (or anyone claiming through them) cannot deny the landlord's title as it stood at the start of the tenancy, and a licensee cannot deny the licensor's title to possession as it stood when the licence was granted.
essential_elements: Tenant estoppel: a tenant, or person claiming through the tenant, cannot deny the landlord had title at the tenancy's commencement -- applies during the tenancy and at any time thereafter.
Licensee estoppel: a person who entered under someone's licence cannot deny that person's title to possession as it stood when the licence was granted.
In both cases the estoppel is fixed to the position at the relevant starting point (tenancy's beginning / licence's grant) -- it doesn't necessarily estop denial of continuing title thereafter.
breakdown.how_to_read: This is a practical, frequently invoked estoppel in landlord-tenant litigation -- a tenant sued for eviction or arrears cannot defend by claiming the landlord never had title, since accepting the tenancy already conceded that point at its inception.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: विबंध का भूस्वामी-किरायेदार और अनुज्ञापक-अनुज्ञप्तिधारी संबंधों पर एक विशिष्ट अनुप्रयोग: किरायेदार (या उसके माध्यम से दावा करने वाला कोई भी व्यक्ति) किरायेदारी के आरंभ में भूस्वामी के हक से इनकार नहीं कर सकता, और अनुज्ञप्तिधारी अनुज्ञा दिए जाने के समय अनुज्ञापक के कब्जे के हक से इनकार नहीं कर सकता।
essential_elements_hi: किरायेदार-विबंध: किरायेदार, या किरायेदार के माध्यम से दावा करने वाला व्यक्ति, यह इनकार नहीं कर सकता कि किरायेदारी के आरंभ में भूस्वामी का हक था -- यह किरायेदारी के दौरान और उसके बाद किसी भी समय लागू होता है।
अनुज्ञप्तिधारी-विबंध: किसी के अनुज्ञा के अंतर्गत प्रवेश करने वाला व्यक्ति यह इनकार नहीं कर सकता कि अनुज्ञा दिए जाने के समय उस व्यक्ति का कब्जे पर हक था।
दोनों मामलों में विबंध प्रासंगिक प्रारंभिक बिंदु (किरायेदारी का आरंभ/अनुज्ञा का अनुदान) पर स्थिति से बंधा है -- यह आवश्यक रूप से बाद में निरंतर हक से इनकार को विबंधित नहीं करता।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह भूस्वामी-किरायेदार वाद-विवाद में एक व्यावहारिक, अक्सर प्रयुक्त विबंध है -- बेदखली या बकाया के लिए मुकदमा किया गया किरायेदार यह दावा करके बचाव नहीं कर सकता कि भूस्वामी का कभी हक नहीं था, क्योंकि किरायेदारी स्वीकार करने से ही उसकी शुरुआत में वह बिंदु पहले ही स्वीकार कर लिया गया था।

sections.title: Estoppel of acceptor of bill of exchange, bailee or licensee
sections.raw_text:
123. No acceptor of a bill of exchange shall be permitted to deny that the drawer had authority to draw such bill or to endorse it; nor shall any bailee or licensee be permitted to deny that his bailor or licensor had, at the time when the bailment or licence commenced, authority to make such bailment or grant such licence.
Explanation 1.—The acceptor of a bill of exchange may deny that the bill was really drawn by the person by whom it purports to have been drawn.
Explanation 2.—If a bailee delivers the goods bailed to a person other than the bailor, he may prove that such person had a right to them as against the bailor.

breakdown.plain_summary: Extends estoppel to commercial and bailment relationships: an acceptor of a bill of exchange cannot deny the drawer's authority to draw/endorse it, and a bailee/licensee cannot deny their bailor/licensor's authority to make the bailment/grant the licence at its commencement -- subject to two clarifying Explanations preserving narrower defences.
essential_elements: Bill of exchange acceptor: estopped from denying the drawer's authority to draw or endorse the bill.
Bailee/licensee: estopped from denying the bailor's/licensor's authority to make the bailment/grant the licence, as it stood when the bailment/licence began.
Explanation 1: the acceptor may still deny the bill was actually drawn by the person it purports to be drawn by -- i.e. may raise a forgery-style defence, distinct from denying authority.
Explanation 2: a bailee who delivers goods to someone other than the bailor may still prove that third person's superior right to the goods as against the bailor -- a jus tertii defence.
breakdown.how_to_read: Closes Chapter VIII. Note how the two Explanations carve out real, substantive defences that remain open despite the general estoppel -- denying genuineness of the instrument itself (Explanation 1) and asserting a third party's superior right (Explanation 2) are conceptually different from denying the counterparty's authority, which is what the estoppel actually forecloses.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: विबंध को वाणिज्यिक और न्यासी संबंधों तक विस्तारित करती है: विनिमय-पत्र का स्वीकर्ता आहर्ता के उसे आहरित/पृष्ठांकित करने के प्राधिकार से इनकार नहीं कर सकता, और न्यासधारी/अनुज्ञप्तिधारी अपने न्यासदाता/अनुज्ञापक के न्यास बनाने/अनुज्ञा देने के प्राधिकार से इसके आरंभ के समय इनकार नहीं कर सकता -- दो स्पष्टीकरणों के अधीन जो संकीर्ण बचाव सुरक्षित रखते हैं।
essential_elements_hi: विनिमय-पत्र का स्वीकर्ता: आहर्ता के पत्र को आहरित या पृष्ठांकित करने के प्राधिकार से इनकार करने से विबंधित।
न्यासधारी/अनुज्ञप्तिधारी: न्यास/अनुज्ञा के आरंभ के समय न्यासदाता/अनुज्ञापक के न्यास बनाने/अनुज्ञा देने के प्राधिकार से इनकार करने से विबंधित।

स्पष्टीकरण 1: स्वीकर्ता फिर भी यह इनकार कर सकता है कि पत्र वास्तव में उस व्यक्ति द्वारा आहरित किया गया था जिसके द्वारा यह आहरित प्रतीत होता है -- अर्थात प्राधिकार से इनकार से भिन्न, कूटरचना-प्रकार का बचाव उठा सकता है।
स्पष्टीकरण 2: न्यासदाता के अलावा किसी अन्य को माल सुपुर्द करने वाला न्यासधारी फिर भी न्यासदाता के विरुद्ध उस तीसरे व्यक्ति के माल पर श्रेष्ठ अधिकार को सिद्ध कर सकता है -- एक जस टर्टी बचाव।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अध्याय VIII को बंद करती है। ध्यान दें कि दोनों स्पष्टीकरण कैसे वास्तविक, मूल बचाव सुरक्षित करते हैं जो सामान्य विबंध के बावजूद खुले रहते हैं -- लिखत की वास्तविकता से इनकार (स्पष्टीकरण 1) और किसी तीसरे पक्ष के श्रेष्ठ अधिकार का दावा (स्पष्टीकरण 2) प्रतिपक्षी के प्राधिकार से इनकार से संकल्पनात्मक रूप से भिन्न हैं, जो विबंध वास्तव में अवरुद्ध करता है।

sections.title: Who may testify
sections.raw_text:
All persons shall be competent to testify unless the Court considers that they are prevented from understanding the questions put to them, or from giving rational answers to those questions, by tender years, extreme old age, disease, whether of body or mind, or any other cause of the same kind.

Explanation.—A person of unsound mind is not incompetent to testify, unless he is prevented by his unsoundness of mind from understanding the questions put to him and giving rational answers to them.

breakdown.plain_summary: The default rule is universal competence: everyone can testify. The only disqualification is functional — an actual, present inability to understand questions or answer rationally, whatever its cause (childhood, old age, illness). It is not a status-based bar.
essential_elements: General rule: all persons are competent witnesses.
Exception is functional, not categorical: incapacity to understand questions or give rational answers.
Cause of incapacity is irrelevant — tender years, extreme old age, physical or mental disease, or any similar cause.
Unsoundness of mind alone does not disqualify; only unsoundness that actually prevents rational testimony does.
exceptions_and_qualifications: A child witness or a person with a mental health condition is not automatically excluded — the Court must test actual capacity, often via preliminary questioning (voir dire).
The bar is high: partial impairment does not disqualify, only impairment severe enough to defeat rational understanding and response.
breakdown.how_to_read: Start from the presumption of competence; only exclude a witness where the Court has actually tested and found incapacity of the specific functional kind described.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: डिफ़ॉल्ट नियम सार्वभौमिक सक्षमता है: हर कोई गवाही दे सकता है। एकमात्र अयोग्यता कार्यात्मक है — प्रश्नों को समझने या तर्कसंगत उत्तर देने की वास्तविक, वर्तमान अक्षमता, चाहे उसका कारण कुछ भी हो (बचपन, वृद्धावस्था, बीमारी)। यह स्थिति-आधारित रोक नहीं है।
essential_elements_hi: सामान्य नियम: सभी व्यक्ति सक्षम गवाह हैं।
अपवाद कार्यात्मक है, श्रेणीबद्ध नहीं: प्रश्नों को समझने या तर्कसंगत उत्तर देने में अक्षमता।
अक्षमता का कारण अप्रासंगिक है — अल्पवय, अत्यधिक वृद्धावस्था, शारीरिक या मानसिक रोग, या कोई समान कारण।
केवल विकृतचित्तता अयोग्य नहीं ठहराती; केवल वह विकृतचित्तता जो वास्तव में तर्कसंगत गवाही को रोकती है, अयोग्य ठहराती है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: बाल गवाह या मानसिक स्वास्थ्य स्थिति वाला व्यक्ति स्वतः बहिष्कृत नहीं है — न्यायालय को वास्तविक क्षमता का परीक्षण करना होगा, अक्सर प्रारंभिक प्रश्नोत्तर (वॉयर डायर) के माध्यम से।
रोक ऊँची है: आंशिक दुर्बलता अयोग्य नहीं ठहराती, केवल तर्कसंगत समझ और प्रतिक्रिया को विफल करने जितनी गंभीर दुर्बलता ही अयोग्य ठहराती है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: सक्षमता की धारणा से शुरू करें; गवाह को केवल तब बहिष्कृत करें जब न्यायालय ने वर्णित विशिष्ट कार्यात्मक प्रकार की अक्षमता का वास्तव में परीक्षण किया हो और पाया हो।

sections.title: Witness unable to communicate verbally
sections.raw_text:
A witness who is unable to speak may give his evidence in any other manner in which he can make it intelligible, as by writing or by signs; but such writing must be written and the signs made in open Court and evidence so given shall be deemed to be oral evidence:

Provided that if the witness is unable to communicate verbally, the Court shall take the assistance of an interpreter or a special educator in recording the statement, and such statement shall be videographed.

breakdown.plain_summary: A witness who cannot speak is not thereby incompetent — they may testify by writing or signs in open Court, and this counts as oral evidence. The 2023 proviso adds a modern safeguard: an interpreter or special educator must assist, and the statement must be videographed.
essential_elements: Applies to witnesses unable to speak.
Evidence may be given by writing or signs, made in open Court.
Such evidence is deemed oral evidence, not documentary.
Proviso (new in BSA): Court must use an interpreter or special educator, and videograph the statement.
exceptions_and_qualifications: The videography requirement is a procedural safeguard new to the BSA — absent from the old Evidence Act — aimed at reliability and protecting vulnerable witnesses.
breakdown.how_to_read: Treat this as making disability no bar to giving oral evidence, with the videography/interpreter proviso as a mandatory modern procedural add-on.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: वह गवाह जो बोल नहीं सकता, इस कारण अक्षम नहीं है — वह लेखन या संकेतों द्वारा खुले न्यायालय में गवाही दे सकता है, और यह मौखिक साक्ष्य के रूप में गिना जाता है। 2023 का परंतुक एक आधुनिक सुरक्षा उपाय जोड़ता है: एक दुभाषिया या विशेष शिक्षक को सहायता करनी चाहिए, और कथन का वीडियोग्राफी किया जाना चाहिए।
essential_elements_hi: बोलने में असमर्थ गवाहों पर लागू होता है।
साक्ष्य लेखन या संकेतों द्वारा दिया जा सकता है, जो खुले न्यायालय में किया जाए।
ऐसी साक्ष्य मौखिक साक्ष्य मानी जाती है, दस्तावेजी नहीं।
परंतुक (बीएसए में नया): न्यायालय को दुभाषिया या विशेष शिक्षक का उपयोग करना चाहिए, और कथन की वीडियोग्राफी करनी चाहिए।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: वीडियोग्राफी की आवश्यकता बीएसए में नई एक प्रक्रियात्मक सुरक्षा है — पुराने साक्ष्य अधिनियम में अनुपस्थित — जिसका उद्देश्य विश्वसनीयता और संवेदनशील गवाहों की सुरक्षा है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इसे यह मानें कि विकलांगता मौखिक साक्ष्य देने में कोई बाधा नहीं है, जिसमें वीडियोग्राफी/दुभाषिया परंतुक एक अनिवार्य आधुनिक प्रक्रियात्मक अतिरिक्त है।

sections.title: Competency of husband and wife as witnesses in certain cases
sections.raw_text:
(1) In all civil proceedings the parties to the suit, and the husband or wife of any party to the suit, shall be competent witnesses.

(2) In criminal proceedings against any person, the husband or wife of such person, respectively, shall be a competent witness.

breakdown.plain_summary: Spouses of parties are competent witnesses — in civil suits for either side, and in criminal proceedings for or against the accused's spouse. This removes any old common-law-style bar on spousal testimony based on marital status alone.
essential_elements: Civil proceedings: parties and their spouses are competent witnesses.
Criminal proceedings: the accused's spouse is a competent witness.
Competence is distinct from compellability and from spousal-communication privilege under s.128.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Competence under s.126 does not override the privilege for marital communications in s.128 — a spouse can testify generally, but cannot be forced to disclose confidential communications made during the marriage.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read s.126 (competence to testify at all) and s.128 (privilege against disclosing marital communications) together — they operate on different questions.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: पक्षकारों के जीवनसाथी सक्षम गवाह हैं — सिविल वादों में दोनों पक्षों के लिए, और आपराधिक कार्यवाहियों में अभियुक्त के जीवनसाथी के लिए या उसके विरुद्ध। यह केवल वैवाहिक स्थिति पर आधारित जीवनसाथी गवाही पर किसी भी पुरानी सामान्य-विधि-शैली की रोक को हटाता है।
essential_elements_hi: सिविल कार्यवाही: पक्षकार और उनके जीवनसाथी सक्षम गवाह हैं।
आपराधिक कार्यवाही: अभियुक्त का जीवनसाथी एक सक्षम गवाह है।
सक्षमता बाध्यता से और धारा 128 के अंतर्गत जीवनसाथी-संसूचना विशेषाधिकार से भिन्न है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: धारा 126 के अंतर्गत सक्षमता धारा 128 में वैवाहिक संसूचनाओं के विशेषाधिकार को अधिक्रमित नहीं करती — जीवनसाथी सामान्यतः गवाही दे सकता है, लेकिन विवाह के दौरान किए गए गोपनीय संसूचनाओं को प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 126 (गवाही देने की सक्षमता) और धारा 128 (वैवाहिक संसूचनाओं को प्रकट न करने का विशेषाधिकार) को साथ पढ़ें — वे अलग-अलग प्रश्नों पर कार्य करते हैं।

sections.title: Judges and Magistrates
sections.raw_text:
No Judge or Magistrate shall, except upon the special order of some Court to which he is subordinate, be compelled to answer any question as to his own conduct in Court as such Judge or Magistrate, or as to anything which came to his knowledge in Court as such Judge or Magistrate; but he may be examined as to other matters which occurred in his presence whilst he was so acting.

Illustrations
(a) A, on his trial before the Court of Session, says that a deposition was improperly taken by B, the Magistrate. B cannot be compelled to answer questions as to this, except upon the special order of a superior Court.
(b) A is accused before the Court of Session of having given false evidence before B, a Magistrate. B cannot be asked what A said, except upon the special order of the superior Court.
(c) A is accused before the Court of Session of attempting to murder a police officer whilst on his trial before B, a Sessions Judge. B may be examined as to what occurred.

breakdown.plain_summary: A judicial officer cannot be compelled to testify about their own judicial conduct or what came to their knowledge while acting judicially, unless a superior court specially orders it. But they can be examined about other things that happened in their presence while on the bench (e.g. an assault in the courtroom).
essential_elements: Protection applies to Judges and Magistrates regarding their own conduct as such.
Compulsion requires special order of a superior/subordinating court.
Carve-out: they may be examined on other matters occurring in their presence while so acting (illustration (c)).
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is a functional immunity protecting judicial independence, not a blanket exemption from being a witness.
breakdown.how_to_read: Distinguish 'conduct as Judge/Magistrate' (protected) from 'other events witnessed while on the bench' (not protected) — illustration (c) is the key dividing example.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: किसी न्यायिक अधिकारी को अपने स्वयं के न्यायिक आचरण या न्यायिक रूप से कार्य करते समय उसके ज्ञान में आई बात के बारे में गवाही देने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, जब तक कोई उच्चतर न्यायालय विशेष रूप से ऐसा आदेश न दे। लेकिन उनकी पीठासीन रहते हुए उनकी उपस्थिति में हुई अन्य बातों (जैसे न्यायालय-कक्ष में हमला) के बारे में उनकी परीक्षा की जा सकती है।
essential_elements_hi: सुरक्षा न्यायाधीशों और मजिस्ट्रेटों पर उनके ऐसे आचरण के संबंध में लागू होती है।
बाध्यता के लिए किसी उच्चतर/अधीनस्थकारी न्यायालय के विशेष आदेश की आवश्यकता है।
अपवाद: उन्हें पीठासीन रहते हुए उनकी उपस्थिति में घटित अन्य मामलों पर परीक्षित किया जा सकता है (उदाहरण (ग))।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह न्यायिक स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा करने वाली एक कार्यात्मक प्रतिरक्षा है, गवाह होने से पूर्ण छूट नहीं।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: 'न्यायाधीश/मजिस्ट्रेट के रूप में आचरण' (संरक्षित) को 'पीठ पर रहते हुए देखी गई अन्य घटनाओं' (असंरक्षित) से अलग करें — उदाहरण (ग) प्रमुख विभाजक उदाहरण है।

sections.title: Communications during marriage
sections.raw_text: No person who is or has been married, shall be compelled to disclose any communication made to him during marriage by any person to whom he is or has been married; nor shall he be permitted to disclose any such communication, unless the person who made it, or his representative in interest, consents, except in suits between married persons, or proceedings in which one married person is prosecuted for any crime committed against the other.

breakdown.plain_summary: Marital communications are privileged both ways: the spouse cannot be compelled to disclose them, and cannot even voluntarily disclose them, without the consent of the spouse who made the communication (or their legal representative) — except in spouse-vs-spouse litigation.
essential_elements: Privilege covers communications made during the marriage (survives after divorce/death for past communications).
Dual bar: cannot be compelled to disclose, and is not permitted to voluntarily disclose.
Waiver requires consent of the communicating spouse or their representative-in-interest.
Exception: suits between married persons, or prosecutions where one spouse is the victim of the other's crime.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Unlike ordinary privileges which the holder alone can waive, here the person who made the communication (not necessarily the witness-spouse) controls the waiver.
breakdown.how_to_read: Treat this as the spousal-privacy counterpart to advocate-client privilege (ss.132-134) — same structure of compelled/voluntary bar with a consent-based waiver and litigation-between-the-parties carve-out.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: वैवाहिक संसूचनाएँ दोनों तरफ से विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त हैं: जीवनसाथी को उन्हें प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, और यहाँ तक कि संसूचना करने वाले जीवनसाथी (या उसके विधिक प्रतिनिधि) की सहमति के बिना स्वेच्छा से भी उन्हें प्रकट नहीं किया जा सकता — सिवाय जीवनसाथी-बनाम-जीवनसाथी वाद-विवाद के।
essential_elements_hi: विशेषाधिकार विवाह के दौरान की गई संसूचनाओं को कवर करता है (विगत संसूचनाओं के लिए तलाक/मृत्यु के बाद भी बना रहता है)।
दोहरी रोक: प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, और स्वेच्छा से प्रकट करने की अनुमति नहीं है।
छूट के लिए संसूचना करने वाले जीवनसाथी या उसके हित-प्रतिनिधि की सहमति आवश्यक है।
अपवाद: विवाहित व्यक्तियों के बीच वाद, या अभियोजन जहाँ एक जीवनसाथी दूसरे के अपराध का पीड़ित हो।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: सामान्य विशेषाधिकारों के विपरीत जिन्हें केवल धारक स्वयं छोड़ सकता है, यहाँ संसूचना करने वाला व्यक्ति (आवश्यक रूप से गवाह-जीवनसाथी नहीं) छूट को नियंत्रित करता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इसे अधिवक्ता-मुवक्किल विशेषाधिकार (धारा 132-134) के जीवनसाथी-गोपनीयता समकक्ष के रूप में मानें — बाध्य/स्वैच्छिक रोक की समान संरचना जिसमें सहमति-आधारित छूट और पक्षों-के-बीच-वाद अपवाद है।

sections.title: Evidence as to affairs of State
sections.raw_text: No one shall be permitted to give any evidence derived from unpublished official records relating to any affairs of State, except with the permission of the officer at the head of the department concerned, who shall give or withhold such permission as he thinks fit.

breakdown.plain_summary: Unpublished government records touching on affairs of State cannot be given in evidence without the head of the concerned department's permission — a form of executive/state privilege, with the department head having unreviewable discretion on the face of the text.
essential_elements: Applies only to unpublished official records relating to affairs of State.
Permission to adduce such evidence rests with the head of the department concerned.
Discretion is framed as the officer's own judgment ('as he thinks fit').
exceptions_and_qualifications: Courts have historically read in some judicial oversight of a blanket claim of privilege under the predecessor provision, especially where the claim is a pretext to hide wrongdoing rather than protect genuine State interest — practitioners should be aware this is litigated, not absolute in practice.
breakdown.how_to_read: Use this section when a party seeks disclosure of internal government files; expect the opposing department to invoke this section and be ready to test whether the document genuinely concerns 'affairs of State'.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: राज्य के कार्यों को स्पर्श करने वाले अप्रकाशित सरकारी अभिलेख संबंधित विभाग के प्रधान की अनुमति के बिना साक्ष्य में नहीं दिए जा सकते — यह कार्यपालक/राज्य विशेषाधिकार का एक रूप है, जिसमें विभाग प्रधान को पाठ के चेहरे पर अपुनरीक्षणीय विवेकाधिकार प्राप्त है।
essential_elements_hi: केवल राज्य के कार्यों से संबंधित अप्रकाशित सरकारी अभिलेखों पर लागू होता है।
ऐसी साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत करने की अनुमति संबंधित विभाग के प्रधान के पास है।
विवेकाधिकार अधिकारी के अपने निर्णय ('जैसा वह उचित समझे') के रूप में तैयार किया गया है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: न्यायालयों ने ऐतिहासिक रूप से पूर्ववर्ती प्रावधान के अंतर्गत विशेषाधिकार के व्यापक दावे की कुछ न्यायिक जांच को पढ़ा है, विशेष रूप से जहाँ दावा वास्तविक राज्य-हित की रक्षा के बजाय गलत कार्य छिपाने का बहाना हो — व्यवसायियों को पता होना चाहिए कि यह व्यवहार में वाद-योग्य है, पूर्ण नहीं।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इस धारा का उपयोग तब करें जब कोई पक्ष आंतरिक सरकारी फाइलों के प्रकटीकरण की मांग करे; प्रतिपक्षी विभाग से इस धारा का आह्वान करने की अपेक्षा करें और यह परखने के लिए तैयार रहें कि दस्तावेज वास्तव में 'राज्य के कार्यों' से संबंधित है या नहीं।

sections.title: Official communications
sections.raw_text: No public officer shall be compelled to disclose communications made to him in official confidence, when he considers that the public interests would suffer by the disclosure.

breakdown.plain_summary: A public officer can refuse to disclose communications received in official confidence if they believe disclosure would harm the public interest — a narrower, officer-level cousin of the department-head privilege in s.129.
essential_elements: Applies to communications made to the officer in official confidence.
Trigger is the officer's own assessment that public interest would suffer.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This is the officer's personal judgment call, distinguishable from s.129's departmental-head gatekeeping over affairs-of-State records generally.
breakdown.how_to_read: Compare with s.129: s.130 is about confidential communications to an officer; s.129 is about unpublished State records more broadly, gated by the department head.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: एक लोक अधिकारी आधिकारिक विश्वास में प्राप्त संसूचनाओं को प्रकट करने से इनकार कर सकता है यदि उसे विश्वास हो कि प्रकटीकरण लोकहित को हानि पहुँचाएगा — यह धारा 129 के विभाग-प्रधान विशेषाधिकार का एक संकीर्ण, अधिकारी-स्तरीय चचेरा भाई है।
essential_elements_hi: अधिकारी को आधिकारिक विश्वास में की गई संसूचनाओं पर लागू होता है।
आरंभक अधिकारी का अपना आकलन है कि लोकहित को हानि होगी।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह अधिकारी का व्यक्तिगत निर्णय है, जो राज्य-कार्यों के अभिलेखों पर सामान्यतः विभाग-प्रधान के द्वारपालन वाली धारा 129 से भिन्न है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 129 से तुलना करें: धारा 130 अधिकारी को की गई गोपनीय संसूचनाओं के बारे में है; धारा 129 व्यापक रूप से अप्रकाशित राज्य अभिलेखों के बारे में है, जो विभाग प्रधान द्वारा नियंत्रित है।

sections.title: Information as to commission of offences
sections.raw_text:
No Magistrate or police officer shall be compelled to say when he got any information as to the commission of any offence, and no revenue officer shall be compelled to say when he got any information as to the commission of any offence against the public revenue.

Explanation.—"revenue officer" means any officer employed in or about the business of any branch of the public revenue.

breakdown.plain_summary: Protects the source/timing of tip-offs to law enforcement: Magistrates, police, and revenue officers cannot be compelled to reveal when (and by extension, often from whom) they received information about an offence — protecting informants.
essential_elements: Covers Magistrates and police officers (any offence) and revenue officers (revenue offences).
Protection is specifically about the timing of receipt of information, which in practice shields the informant.
exceptions_and_qualifications: This underpins informer protection in criminal investigations — relevant in bail and disclosure disputes where the defence seeks informant identity.
breakdown.how_to_read: Use this section to resist defence attempts to unmask police informants via questions about when/how a tip was received.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: कानून प्रवर्तन को मिली सूचनाओं के स्रोत/समय की रक्षा करती है: मजिस्ट्रेट, पुलिस, और राजस्व अधिकारियों को यह प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता कि उन्हें किसी अपराध के बारे में सूचना कब मिली (और इसके विस्तार से, अक्सर किससे मिली) — सूचनादाताओं की रक्षा करते हुए।
essential_elements_hi: मजिस्ट्रेट और पुलिस अधिकारियों (किसी भी अपराध) और राजस्व अधिकारियों (राजस्व अपराध) को कवर करती है।
सुरक्षा विशेष रूप से सूचना प्राप्ति के समय के बारे में है, जो व्यवहार में सूचनादाता की रक्षा करती है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह आपराधिक अन्वेषणों में सूचनादाता सुरक्षा का आधार है — जमानत और प्रकटीकरण विवादों में प्रासंगिक जहाँ बचाव पक्ष सूचनादाता की पहचान चाहता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इस धारा का उपयोग तब करें जब बचाव पक्ष सूचना कब/कैसे प्राप्त हुई इस बारे में प्रश्नों के माध्यम से पुलिस सूचनादाताओं को बेनकाब करने का प्रयास करे।

sections.title: Professional communications
sections.raw_text:
(1) No advocate, shall at any time be permitted, unless with his client's express consent, to disclose any communication made to him in the course and for the purpose of his service as such advocate, by or on behalf of his client, or to state the contents or condition of any document with which he has become acquainted in the course and for the purpose of his professional service, or to disclose any advice given by him to his client in the course and for the purpose of such service:

Provided that nothing in this section shall protect from disclosure of—
(a) any such communication made in furtherance of any illegal purpose;
(b) any fact observed by any advocate, in the course of his service as such, showing that any crime or fraud has been committed since the commencement of his service.

(2) It is immaterial whether the attention of such advocate referred to in the proviso to sub-section (1), was or was not directed to such fact by or on behalf of his client.

Explanation.—The obligation stated in this section continues after the professional service has ceased.

Illustrations
(a) A, a client, says to B, an advocate—"I have committed forgery, and I wish you to defend me". As the defence of a man known to be guilty is not a criminal purpose, this communication is protected from disclosure.
(b) A, a client, says to B, an advocate—"I wish to obtain possession of property by the use of a forged deed on which I request you to sue". This communication, being made in furtherance of a criminal purpose, is not protected from disclosure.
(c) A, being charged with embezzlement, retains B, an advocate, to defend him. In the course of the proceedings, B observes that an entry has been made in A's account book, charging A with the sum said to have been embezzled, which entry was not in the book at the commencement of his professional service. This being a fact observed by B in the course of his service, showing that a fraud has been committed since the commencement of the proceedings, it is not protected from disclosure.

(3) The provisions of this section shall apply to interpreters, and the clerks or employees of advocates.

breakdown.plain_summary: This is the core advocate-client privilege: an advocate cannot disclose client communications, document contents learned professionally, or advice given, without the client's express consent. Two carve-outs pierce it — communications furthering an illegal purpose, and facts showing crime or fraud committed since the advocate's engagement began. The privilege survives the end of the engagement and extends to interpreters, clerks, and employees of advocates.
essential_elements: Bars disclosure of client communications, document contents, and advice given in course of professional service.
Waiver requires client's express consent.
Exception (a): communications made in furtherance of an illegal purpose — e.g. planning a future crime, not confessing a past one.
Exception (b): facts observed by the advocate showing crime/fraud committed since the engagement began — irrespective of whether the client drew attention to it (sub-section (2)).
Privilege survives termination of the professional relationship (Explanation).
Extends to interpreters and the advocate's clerks/employees (sub-section (3)).
exceptions_and_qualifications: The classic illustration-(a)/(b) distinction: confessing past guilt while seeking defence is protected; instructing the lawyer to commit a future fraud (e.g. suing on a forged deed) is not.
This is the single most litigated privilege in practice — disputes usually turn on whether communications fall within exception (a) or (b).
breakdown.how_to_read: Anchor on illustrations (a)-(c): they are the exam/courtroom test for where the privilege ends and the illegal-purpose/ongoing-fraud exceptions begin.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: यह मूल अधिवक्ता-मुवक्किल विशेषाधिकार है: एक अधिवक्ता मुवक्किल की सहमति के बिना मुवक्किल की संसूचनाएँ, पेशेवर रूप से सीखी गई दस्तावेज सामग्री, या दी गई सलाह प्रकट नहीं कर सकता। दो अपवाद इसे भेदते हैं — गैरकानूनी उद्देश्य को आगे बढ़ाने वाली संसूचनाएँ, और अधिवक्ता के जुड़ाव के बाद से किए गए अपराध या कपट दिखाने वाले तथ्य। विशेषाधिकार जुड़ाव की समाप्ति के बाद भी बना रहता है और अधिवक्ताओं के दुभाषियों, लिपिकों और कर्मचारियों तक विस्तारित होता है।
essential_elements_hi: पेशेवर सेवा के क्रम में मुवक्किल की संसूचनाओं, दस्तावेज सामग्री, और दी गई सलाह के प्रकटीकरण को रोकती है।
छूट के लिए मुवक्किल की स्पष्ट सहमति आवश्यक है।
अपवाद (क): गैरकानूनी उद्देश्य को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए की गई संसूचनाएँ — जैसे भविष्य के अपराध की योजना बनाना, भूतकाल के अपराध को स्वीकार करना नहीं।
अपवाद (ख): अधिवक्ता द्वारा देखे गए तथ्य जो जुड़ाव शुरू होने के बाद से किए गए अपराध/कपट को दिखाते हैं — चाहे मुवक्किल ने उस पर ध्यान आकर्षित किया हो या नहीं (उपधारा (2))।
विशेषाधिकार पेशेवर संबंध की समाप्ति के बाद भी बना रहता है (स्पष्टीकरण)।
दुभाषियों और अधिवक्ता के लिपिकों/कर्मचारियों तक विस्तारित होता है (उपधारा (3))।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: क्लासिक उदाहरण-(क)/(ख) भेद: बचाव चाहते हुए भूतकाल के दोष को स्वीकार करना संरक्षित है; वकील को भविष्य में कपट करने का निर्देश देना (जैसे कूटरचित विलेख पर मुकदमा करना) संरक्षित नहीं है।
व्यवहार में यह एकमात्र सबसे अधिक वाद-योग्य विशेषाधिकार है — विवाद आमतौर पर इस पर घूमते हैं कि संसूचनाएँ अपवाद (क) या (ख) के अंतर्गत आती हैं या नहीं।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: उदाहरण (क)-(ग) पर आधार रखें: वे यह परखने के लिए परीक्षा-न्यायालय कसौटी हैं कि विशेषाधिकार कहाँ समाप्त होता है और गैरकानूनी-उद्देश्य/चालू-कपट अपवाद कहाँ शुरू होते हैं।

sections.title: Privilege not waived by volunteering evidence
sections.raw_text: If any party to a suit gives evidence therein at his own instance or otherwise, he shall not be deemed to have consented thereby to such disclosure as is mentioned in section 132; and, if any party to a suit or proceeding calls any such advocate, as a witness, he shall be deemed to have consented to such disclosure only if he questions such advocate, on matters which, but for such question, he would not be at liberty to disclose.

breakdown.plain_summary: A client testifying in their own case does not automatically waive advocate-client privilege. Waiver by calling one's own advocate as a witness is narrow — it only extends to whatever specific matters the client actually questions the advocate about that would otherwise be privileged.
essential_elements: Giving evidence generally does not imply consent to disclosure under s.132.
Calling one's advocate as a witness implies consent only to the specific privileged matters actually put in question.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Practitioners should question their own advocate-witness narrowly to avoid inadvertently waiving privilege beyond what is intended.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read as a waiver-scoping rule: it prevents accidental blanket waiver of s.132 privilege merely by testifying or calling one's lawyer.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अपने ही मामले में गवाही देने वाला मुवक्किल स्वतः अधिवक्ता-मुवक्किल विशेषाधिकार नहीं छोड़ता। अपने अधिवक्ता को गवाह के रूप में बुलाने से छूट संकीर्ण है — यह केवल उन विशिष्ट मामलों तक विस्तारित होती है जिनके बारे में मुवक्किल वास्तव में अधिवक्ता से प्रश्न पूछता है जो अन्यथा विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त होते।
essential_elements_hi: सामान्यतः गवाही देना धारा 132 के अंतर्गत प्रकटीकरण की सहमति का तात्पर्य नहीं रखता।
अपने अधिवक्ता को गवाह के रूप में बुलाना केवल उन विशिष्ट विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त मामलों की सहमति का तात्पर्य रखता है जो वास्तव में प्रश्नगत किए जाते हैं।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: व्यवसायियों को अपने अधिवक्ता-गवाह से संकीर्ण रूप से प्रश्न पूछना चाहिए ताकि इच्छित से परे विशेषाधिकार की अनजाने छूट से बचा जा सके।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इसे छूट-सीमांकन नियम के रूप में पढ़ें: यह केवल गवाही देने या अपने वकील को बुलाने मात्र से धारा 132 विशेषाधिकार की आकस्मिक व्यापक छूट को रोकता है।

sections.title: Confidential communications with legal advisers
sections.raw_text: No one shall be compelled to disclose to the Court any confidential communication which has taken place between him and his legal adviser, unless he offers himself as a witness, in which case he may be compelled to disclose any such communications as may appear to the Court necessary to be known in order to explain any evidence which he has given, but no others.

breakdown.plain_summary: This is the client-side mirror of s.132's advocate-side privilege: the client cannot be compelled to disclose confidential communications with their legal adviser, unless they testify, in which case disclosure is compelled only to the extent necessary to explain evidence they have given.
essential_elements: Default: client cannot be compelled to disclose confidential legal-adviser communications.
If client testifies, compelled disclosure is limited to what is necessary to explain the evidence actually given — not a general waiver.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Read together with ss.132-133: s.132 binds the advocate, s.134 binds/protects the client, s.133 governs what testifying does to the s.132 privilege.
breakdown.how_to_read: Think of ss.132-134 as one privilege with two mouths (advocate and client) that can each assert it, and a carefully scoped waiver mechanism.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: यह धारा 132 के अधिवक्ता-पक्षीय विशेषाधिकार का मुवक्किल-पक्षीय प्रतिबिंब है: मुवक्किल को अपने विधिक सलाहकार के साथ गोपनीय संसूचनाओं को प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, जब तक वह गवाही न दे, जिस स्थिति में प्रकटीकरण केवल उसकी दी गई साक्ष्य को स्पष्ट करने के लिए आवश्यक सीमा तक बाध्य किया जाता है।
essential_elements_hi: डिफ़ॉल्ट: मुवक्किल को गोपनीय विधिक-सलाहकार संसूचनाओं को प्रकट करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता।
यदि मुवक्किल गवाही देता है, तो बाध्य प्रकटीकरण उसकी वास्तव में दी गई साक्ष्य को स्पष्ट करने के लिए आवश्यक तक सीमित है — सामान्य छूट नहीं।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: धारा 132-133 के साथ साथ पढ़ें: धारा 132 अधिवक्ता को बाँधती है, धारा 134 मुवक्किल को बाँधती/रक्षा करती है, धारा 133 यह नियंत्रित करती है कि गवाही देना धारा 132 विशेषाधिकार पर क्या प्रभाव डालता है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 132-134 को दो मुँह (अधिवक्ता और मुवक्किल) वाले एक विशेषाधिकार के रूप में सोचें जो प्रत्येक इसका दावा कर सकते हैं, और एक सावधानीपूर्वक सीमांकित छूट तंत्र के साथ।

sections.title: Production of title-deeds of witness not a party
sections.raw_text: No witness who is not a party to a suit shall be compelled to produce his title-deeds to any property, or any document in virtue of which he holds any property as pledgee or mortgagee or any document the production of which might tend to criminate him, unless he has agreed in writing to produce them with the person seeking the production of such deeds or some person through whom he claims.

breakdown.plain_summary: A non-party witness cannot be forced to produce their own title-deeds, pledge/mortgage documents, or self-incriminating documents, unless they have already agreed in writing to produce them (with the party seeking production or someone through whom that party claims).
essential_elements: Protection applies only to witnesses who are not parties to the suit.
Covers title-deeds, pledgee/mortgagee documents, and self-incriminating documents.
Exception: a prior written agreement to produce, made with the requesting party or their predecessor-in-title.
breakdown.how_to_read: Use to protect a non-party witness's property documents from compelled production absent a pre-existing written agreement to produce.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: एक गैर-पक्षकार गवाह को अपने स्वयं के हक-विलेख, बंधक/गिरवी दस्तावेज, या आत्म-दोषारोपक दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, जब तक वह पहले ही लिखित रूप में उन्हें प्रस्तुत करने पर सहमत न हो चुका हो (प्रस्तुति चाहने वाले पक्ष के साथ या किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति के साथ जिसके माध्यम से वह पक्ष दावा करता है)।
essential_elements_hi: सुरक्षा केवल उन गवाहों पर लागू होती है जो वाद के पक्षकार नहीं हैं।
हक-विलेख, गिरवीदार/बंधकदार दस्तावेज, और आत्म-दोषारोपक दस्तावेजों को कवर करती है।
अपवाद: अनुरोध करने वाले पक्ष या उसके हक-पूर्ववर्ती के साथ प्रस्तुत करने के लिए पूर्व लिखित करार।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: किसी गैर-पक्षकार गवाह के संपत्ति दस्तावेजों को प्रस्तुत करने के लिए पूर्व-विद्यमान लिखित करार के अभाव में बाध्य प्रस्तुति से बचाने के लिए उपयोग करें।

sections.title: Production of documents or electronic records which another person, having possession, could refuse to produce
sections.raw_text: No one shall be compelled to produce documents in his possession or electronic records under his control, which any other person would be entitled to refuse to produce if they were in his possession or control, unless such last-mentioned person consents to their production.

breakdown.plain_summary: A derivative protection: if the true owner/interested party could refuse to produce a document, the person who currently merely holds it also cannot be compelled to produce it, unless the owner consents.
essential_elements: Applies to documents in possession or electronic records under a person's control.
The test is whether a third party (the person who would otherwise be entitled to refuse) consents.
breakdown.how_to_read: Think of this as privilege 'following' the document to whoever holds it, protecting the true interest-holder's refusal right even when someone else has physical custody.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: एक व्युत्पन्न सुरक्षा: यदि वास्तविक स्वामी/हितबद्ध पक्ष किसी दस्तावेज को प्रस्तुत करने से इनकार कर सकता है, तो जो व्यक्ति वर्तमान में केवल उसे धारण करता है वह भी उसे प्रस्तुत करने के लिए बाध्य नहीं किया जा सकता, जब तक स्वामी सहमति न दे।
essential_elements_hi: किसी व्यक्ति के कब्जे में दस्तावेजों या उसके नियंत्रण में इलेक्ट्रॉनिक अभिलेखों पर लागू होती है।
कसौटी यह है कि क्या तीसरा पक्ष (वह व्यक्ति जो अन्यथा इनकार करने का हकदार होता) सहमत है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इसे विशेषाधिकार के दस्तावेज का 'अनुसरण' करने के रूप में सोचें चाहे वह किसी के भी पास हो, वास्तविक हितधारक के इनकार अधिकार की रक्षा करते हुए भले ही किसी और के पास भौतिक अभिरक्षा हो।

sections.title: Witness not excused from answering on ground that answer will criminate
sections.raw_text:
A witness shall not be excused from answering any question as to any matter relevant to the matter in issue in any suit or in any civil or criminal proceeding, upon the ground that the answer to such question will criminate, or may tend directly or indirectly to criminate, such witness, or that it will expose, or tend directly or indirectly to expose, such witness to a penalty or forfeiture of any kind:

Provided that no such answer, which a witness shall be compelled to give, shall subject him to any arrest or prosecution, or be proved against him in any criminal proceeding, except a prosecution for giving false evidence by such answer.

breakdown.plain_summary: A witness cannot dodge a relevant question merely because the truthful answer would incriminate them or expose them to penalty — but in exchange, the law grants 'use immunity': that compelled answer cannot later be used to arrest, prosecute, or convict them (except for perjury on that very answer).
essential_elements: General rule: relevance overrides the self-incrimination objection — a witness must answer.
Proviso grants use immunity: the compelled answer cannot found arrest, prosecution, or be proved against the witness in any criminal proceeding.
Sole exception to the immunity: a prosecution for giving false evidence by that very answer (perjury).
exceptions_and_qualifications: This trades away the witness's right to silence on relevance grounds in exchange for a shield against the answer's use — distinct from and narrower than a blanket immunity from all future prosecution on the underlying conduct.
breakdown.how_to_read: Pair the compulsion-to-answer rule with its counterweight proviso — witnesses are examined on the trade-off between compelled testimony and use immunity, not on an absolute privilege against self-incrimination in the witness-box.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: कोई गवाह केवल इसलिए किसी प्रासंगिक प्रश्न का उत्तर देने से बच नहीं सकता कि सच्चा उत्तर उसे दोषी ठहराएगा या दंड के लिए उजागर करेगा — लेकिन बदले में, कानून 'उपयोग प्रतिरक्षा' देता है: उस बाध्य उत्तर का उपयोग बाद में उसे गिरफ्तार करने, अभियोजित करने, या दोषसिद्ध करने के लिए नहीं किया जा सकता (उस उत्तर पर झूठी गवाही के अपराध को छोड़कर)।
essential_elements_hi: सामान्य नियम: प्रासंगिकता आत्म-दोषारोपण आपत्ति पर प्रबल होती है — गवाह को उत्तर देना होगा।
परंतुक उपयोग प्रतिरक्षा देता है: बाध्य उत्तर गिरफ्तारी, अभियोजन का आधार नहीं बन सकता, और न ही किसी आपराधिक कार्यवाही में गवाह के विरुद्ध सिद्ध किया जा सकता है।
प्रतिरक्षा का एकमात्र अपवाद: उसी उत्तर द्वारा झूठी साक्ष्य देने (झूठी गवाही) के लिए अभियोजन।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह उत्तर के उपयोग के विरुद्ध एक ढाल के बदले प्रासंगिकता आधार पर गवाह के मौन रहने के अधिकार का व्यापार करता है — यह अंतर्निहित आचरण पर सभी भविष्य के अभियोजन से पूर्ण प्रतिरक्षा से भिन्न और संकीर्ण है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: उत्तर देने की बाध्यता के नियम को उसके प्रतिसंतुलक परंतुक के साथ जोड़ें — गवाहों की जांच बाध्य गवाही और उपयोग प्रतिरक्षा के बीच व्यापार-व्यवस्था पर होती है, न कि गवाह-कटघरे में आत्म-दोषारोपण के विरुद्ध पूर्ण विशेषाधिकार पर।

sections.title: Accomplice
sections.raw_text: An accomplice shall be a competent witness against an accused person; and a conviction is not illegal if it proceeds upon the corroborated testimony of an accomplice.

breakdown.plain_summary: An accomplice can testify against a co-accused, and a conviction based on corroborated accomplice testimony is legally valid — the statute doesn't forbid it, though courts as a rule of prudence generally look for corroboration before relying on uncorroborated accomplice evidence.
essential_elements: Accomplices are competent witnesses against an accused.
Conviction on corroborated accomplice testimony is not illegal.
exceptions_and_qualifications: The section validates corroborated accomplice evidence; it does not say uncorroborated accomplice evidence is inadmissible — but courts, as a matter of prudence (read with the presumption in s.119), are cautious about convicting on wholly uncorroborated accomplice testimony alone.
breakdown.how_to_read: Read with s.119(1)(b)'s illustrative presumption that an accomplice is unworthy of credit unless corroborated — the two sections together drive the corroboration-in-practice rule.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: एक सहअपराधी सह-अभियुक्त के विरुद्ध गवाही दे सकता है, और संपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य पर आधारित दोषसिद्धि विधिक रूप से वैध है — कानून इसे वर्जित नहीं करता, हालाँकि न्यायालय विवेक के नियम के रूप में सामान्यतः असंपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य पर भरोसा करने से पहले संपुष्टि खोजते हैं।
essential_elements_hi: सहअपराधी अभियुक्त के विरुद्ध सक्षम गवाह हैं।
संपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य पर दोषसिद्धि अवैध नहीं है।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: यह धारा संपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य को वैध ठहराती है; यह नहीं कहती कि असंपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य अस्वीकार्य है — लेकिन न्यायालय, विवेक के मामले के रूप में (धारा 119 की धारणा के साथ पढ़ा जाए), पूर्णतः असंपुष्ट सहअपराधी साक्ष्य के आधार पर अकेले दोषसिद्ध करने में सतर्क रहते हैं।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: धारा 119(1)(ख) की उदाहरणात्मक धारणा के साथ पढ़ें कि सहअपराधी तब तक विश्वास के योग्य नहीं माना जाता जब तक संपुष्ट न हो — दोनों धाराएँ मिलकर व्यवहार में संपुष्टि नियम को संचालित करती हैं।

sections.title: Number of witnesses
sections.raw_text: No particular number of witnesses shall in any case be required for the proof of any fact.

breakdown.plain_summary: There is no minimum-witness-count rule under Indian evidence law — a single credible witness's testimony can prove a fact; quality, not quantity, governs.
essential_elements: No statutory minimum number of witnesses is needed to prove any fact.
breakdown.how_to_read: Cite this to rebut arguments that a case must fail merely for having 'only one witness' — the touchstone is credibility, not headcount.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: भारतीय साक्ष्य विधि के अंतर्गत कोई न्यूनतम-गवाह-संख्या नियम नहीं है — एक विश्वसनीय गवाह की गवाही किसी तथ्य को सिद्ध कर सकती है; गुणवत्ता, मात्रा नहीं, निर्णायक होती है।
essential_elements_hi: किसी भी तथ्य को सिद्ध करने के लिए कोई संवैधिक न्यूनतम गवाह संख्या आवश्यक नहीं है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: इस धारा को इस तर्क का खंडन करने के लिए उद्धृत करें कि किसी मामले में केवल 'एक गवाह' होने मात्र से वह विफल होना चाहिए — कसौटी विश्वसनीयता है, गिनती नहीं।

sections.title: Order of production and examination of witnesses
sections.raw_text: The order in which witnesses are produced and examined shall be regulated by the law and practice for the time being relating to civil and criminal procedure respectively, and, in the absence of any such law, by the discretion of the Court.

breakdown.plain_summary: The BSA doesn't itself fix witness order — that's left to the applicable procedural law (CPC for civil, BNSS for criminal), and failing any specific rule, to the trial Court's discretion.
essential_elements: Order of witnesses is governed by procedural law (civil or criminal, as applicable).
Residual discretion vests in the Court where no procedural rule governs.
breakdown.how_to_read: This is a signpost section — it defers to CPC/BNSS rather than legislating witness sequencing itself; don't expect substantive content here beyond the deferral.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: बीएसए स्वयं गवाह क्रम तय नहीं करता — वह लागू प्रक्रियात्मक विधि (सिविल के लिए सीपीसी, आपराधिक के लिए बीएनएसएस) पर छोड़ दिया गया है, और किसी विशिष्ट नियम के अभाव में, विचारण न्यायालय के विवेक पर।
essential_elements_hi: गवाहों का क्रम प्रक्रियात्मक विधि (जैसा लागू हो, सिविल या आपराधिक) द्वारा शासित है।
जहाँ कोई प्रक्रियात्मक नियम शासित नहीं करता वहाँ अवशिष्ट विवेक न्यायालय में निहित है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह एक संकेत-पट्ट धारा है — यह स्वयं गवाह अनुक्रम को विधायित करने के बजाय सीपीसी/बीएनएसएस पर स्थगित करती है; यहाँ स्थगन से परे मूल विषयवस्तु की अपेक्षा न करें।

sections.title: Judge to decide as to admissibility of evidence
sections.raw_text:
(1) When either party proposes to give evidence of any fact, the Judge may ask the party proposing to give the evidence in what manner the alleged fact, if proved, would be relevant; and the Judge shall admit the evidence if he thinks that the fact, if proved, would be relevant, and not otherwise.

(2) If the fact proposed to be proved is one of which evidence is admissible only upon proof of some other fact, such last mentioned fact must be proved before evidence is given of the fact first mentioned, unless the party undertakes to give proof of such fact, and the Court is satisfied with such undertaking.

(3) If the relevancy of one alleged fact depends upon another alleged fact being first proved, the Judge may, in his discretion, either permit evidence of the first fact to be given before the second fact is proved, or require evidence to be given of the second fact before evidence is given of the first fact.

Illustrations
(a) It is proposed to prove a statement about a relevant fact by a person alleged to be dead, which statement is relevant under section 26. The fact that the person is dead must be proved by the person proposing to prove the statement, before evidence is given of the statement.
(b) It is proposed to prove, by a copy, the contents of a document said to be lost. The fact that the original is lost must be proved by the person proposing to produce the copy, before the copy is produced.
(c) A is accused of receiving stolen property knowing it to have been stolen. It is proposed to prove that he denied the possession of the property. The relevancy of the denial depends on the identity of the property. The Court may, in its discretion, either require the property to be identified before the denial of the possession is proved, or permit the denial of the possession to be proved before the property is identified.
(d) It is proposed to prove a fact A which is said to have been the cause or effect of a fact in issue. There are several intermediate facts B, C and D which must be shown to exist before the fact A can be regarded as the cause or effect of the fact in issue. The Court may either permit A to be proved before B, C or D is proved, or may require proof of B, C and D before permitting proof of A.

breakdown.plain_summary: The trial Judge gatekeeps admissibility by testing relevance before evidence goes in, and manages the sequencing problem of 'conditional facts' — where a fact is only relevant/admissible once some foundational fact is proved (e.g. proving a person is dead before admitting their dying declaration-style statement).
essential_elements: Judge tests relevance of proposed evidence before admitting it (sub-section (1)).

Where admissibility of Fact A depends on Fact B being proved first, Fact B ordinarily must be proved first, unless the party undertakes to prove it and the Court accepts the undertaking (sub-section (2)).
Where relevancy (not admissibility) is conditional on another fact, the Judge has discretion on the order of proof (sub-section (3)).
Four illustrations model this: unavailable-declarant statements, lost-document copies, stolen-property identification, and multi-link causation chains.
exceptions_and_qualifications: Sub-section (2) (foundational fact for admissibility) is stricter than sub-section (3) (foundational fact for relevancy only) — the former generally requires proof first unless the Court accepts an undertaking; the latter is squarely discretionary.
breakdown.how_to_read: This is the 'conditional relevance' engine of the Adhiniyam — map any foundational-fact dispute (dead declarant, lost document, disputed identity) onto sub-sections (2)/(3) using the illustrations as templates.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: विचारण न्यायाधीश साक्ष्य के प्रवेश से पहले प्रासंगिकता का परीक्षण करके स्वीकार्यता का द्वारपालन करते हैं, और 'सशर्त तथ्यों' की अनुक्रमण समस्या का प्रबंधन करते हैं — जहाँ कोई तथ्य केवल तभी प्रासंगिक/स्वीकार्य होता है जब कोई आधारभूत तथ्य सिद्ध हो जाए (जैसे मृत्यु-कालिक कथन-शैली के कथन को स्वीकार करने से पहले व्यक्ति के मृत होने को सिद्ध करना)।
essential_elements_hi: न्यायाधीश प्रस्तावित साक्ष्य को स्वीकार करने से पहले उसकी प्रासंगिकता का परीक्षण करता है (उपधारा (1))।

जहाँ तथ्य क की स्वीकार्यता तथ्य ख के पहले सिद्ध होने पर निर्भर करती है, वहाँ सामान्यतः तथ्य ख को पहले सिद्ध करना होगा, जब तक पक्ष उसे सिद्ध करने का वचन न दे और न्यायालय उस वचन को स्वीकार न करे (उपधारा (2))।
जहाँ प्रासंगिकता (स्वीकार्यता नहीं) किसी अन्य तथ्य पर सशर्त हो, वहाँ न्यायाधीश को सिद्ध करने के क्रम पर विवेक है (उपधारा (3))।
चार उदाहरण इसका प्रतिरूपण करते हैं: अनुपलब्ध-कथनकर्ता के कथन, खोए दस्तावेज की प्रतियाँ, चोरी की संपत्ति की पहचान, और बहु-कड़ी कार्यकारण शृंखलाएँ।
exceptions_and_qualifications_hi: उपधारा (2) (स्वीकार्यता के लिए आधारभूत तथ्य) उपधारा (3) (केवल प्रासंगिकता के लिए आधारभूत तथ्य) से अधिक सख्त है — पहली को सामान्यतः पहले सिद्ध करना आवश्यक है जब तक न्यायालय वचन स्वीकार न करे; दूसरी पूर्णतः विवेकाधीन है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह अधिनियम का 'सशर्त प्रासंगिकता' इंजन है — किसी भी आधारभूत-तथ्य विवाद (मृत कथनकर्ता, खोया दस्तावेज, विवादित पहचान) को उदाहरणों को टेम्पलेट के रूप में उपयोग करते हुए उपधारा (2)/(3) पर मानचित्रित करें।

sections.title: Examination of witnesses
sections.raw_text:
(1) The examination of a witness by the party who calls him shall be called his examination-in-chief.

(2) The examination of a witness by the adverse party shall be called his cross-examination.

(3) The examination of a witness, subsequent to the cross-examination, by the party who called him, shall be called his re-examination.

breakdown.plain_summary: Defines the three stages of witness examination by name: examination-in-chief (calling party), cross-examination (adverse party), re-examination (calling party again, after cross).
essential_elements: Examination-in-chief: by the party who called the witness.
Cross-examination: by the adverse party.
Re-examination: by the calling party, after cross-examination.
breakdown.how_to_read: Foundational vocabulary section — every subsequent section in this Chapter (order, scope, leading questions) builds on these three defined stages.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: गवाह परीक्षा के तीन चरणों को नाम से परिभाषित करती है: मुख्य परीक्षा (बुलाने वाला पक्ष), प्रति-परीक्षा (प्रतिकूल पक्ष), पुनः परीक्षा (बुलाने वाला पक्ष फिर से, प्रति-परीक्षा के बाद)।
essential_elements_hi: मुख्य परीक्षा: गवाह को बुलाने वाले पक्ष द्वारा।
प्रति-परीक्षा: प्रतिकूल पक्ष द्वारा।
पुनः परीक्षा: प्रति-परीक्षा के बाद, बुलाने वाले पक्ष द्वारा।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: यह आधारभूत शब्दावली धारा है — इस अध्याय की बाद की हर धारा (क्रम, दायरा, सुझावात्मक प्रश्न) इन तीन परिभाषित चरणों पर निर्मित है।

sections.title: Order of examinations
sections.raw_text:
(1) Witnesses shall be first examined-in-chief, then (if the adverse party so desires) cross-examined, then (if the party calling him so desires) re-examined.

(2) The examination-in-chief and cross-examination must relate to relevant facts, but the cross-examination need not be confined to the facts to which the witness testified on his examination-in-chief.

(3) The re-examination shall be directed to the explanation of matters referred to in cross-examination; and, if new matter is, by permission of the Court, introduced in re-examination, the adverse party may further cross-examine upon that matter.

breakdown.plain_summary: Fixes the sequence (chief → cross → re-examination) and the scope rules for each: chief and cross must stick to relevant facts, but cross can range beyond what was covered in chief; re-examination is normally confined to explaining cross-examination points, with new matter allowed only with Court permission (which then reopens cross-examination on that new matter).
essential_elements: Fixed order: examination-in-chief, then cross-examination (if desired), then re-examination (if desired).
Chief and cross must relate to relevant facts.
Cross-examination is not confined to the topics raised in chief — it can range wider (within relevance).
Re-examination is normally limited to explaining matters raised in cross.
New matter in re-examination requires Court permission, and triggers a further right of cross-examination on that new matter for the adverse party.
breakdown.how_to_read: The key asymmetry to remember: cross-examination is broader than chief (can go beyond chief's topics), while re-examination is narrower (confined to explaining cross) unless the Court specially allows new matter.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: अनुक्रम (मुख्य → प्रति → पुनः परीक्षा) और प्रत्येक के लिए दायरा नियम तय करती है: मुख्य और प्रति-परीक्षा प्रासंगिक तथ्यों तक सीमित रहनी चाहिए, लेकिन प्रति-परीक्षा मुख्य में कवर किए गए से आगे जा सकती है; पुनः परीक्षा सामान्यतः प्रति-परीक्षा बिंदुओं को स्पष्ट करने तक सीमित है, नई सामग्री केवल न्यायालय की अनुमति से अनुमत है (जो फिर उस नई सामग्री पर प्रति-परीक्षा को पुनः खोलती है)।
essential_elements_hi: निश्चित क्रम: मुख्य परीक्षा, फिर प्रति-परीक्षा (यदि इच्छित हो), फिर पुनः परीक्षा (यदि इच्छित हो)।
मुख्य और प्रति-परीक्षा प्रासंगिक तथ्यों से संबंधित होनी चाहिए।
प्रति-परीक्षा मुख्य में उठाए गए विषयों तक सीमित नहीं है — यह (प्रासंगिकता की सीमा के भीतर) व्यापक रूप से फैल सकती है।
पुनः परीक्षा सामान्यतः प्रति-परीक्षा में उठाए गए मामलों को स्पष्ट करने तक सीमित है।
पुनः परीक्षा में नई सामग्री के लिए न्यायालय की अनुमति आवश्यक है, और यह उस नई सामग्री पर प्रतिकूल पक्ष के लिए आगे प्रति-परीक्षा के अधिकार को ट्रिगर करती है।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: याद रखने योग्य मुख्य असमानता: प्रति-परीक्षा मुख्य से अधिक व्यापक है (मुख्य के विषयों से आगे जा सकती है), जबकि पुनः परीक्षा संकीर्ण है (प्रति को स्पष्ट करने तक सीमित) जब तक न्यायालय विशेष रूप से नई सामग्री की अनुमति न दे।

sections.title: Cross-examination of person called to produce a document
sections.raw_text: A person summoned to produce a document does not become a witness by the mere fact that he produces it, and cannot be cross-examined unless and until he is called as a witness.

breakdown.plain_summary: Merely producing a document in response to a summons does not turn someone into a witness subject to cross-examination — they must actually be called as a witness first.
essential_elements: Production of a document alone does not confer witness status.
Cross-examination is only permissible once the person is formally called as a witness.
breakdown.how_to_read: Useful shield for custodians/record-keepers who produce documents under summons without wanting to be drawn into the witness box and cross-examined.
breakdown.plain_summary_hi: केवल समन के जवाब में दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करना किसी को प्रति-परीक्षा के अधीन गवाह नहीं बनाता — उसे पहले वास्तव में गवाह के रूप में बुलाया जाना चाहिए।
essential_elements_hi: अकेले दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करना गवाह दर्जा प्रदान नहीं करता।
प्रति-परीक्षा केवल तभी अनुमेय है जब व्यक्ति को औपचारिक रूप से गवाह के रूप में बुलाया गया हो।
breakdown.how_to_read_hi: अभिरक्षकों/अभिलेख-रखवालों के लिए उपयोगी ढाल जो समन के अंतर्गत दस्तावेज प्रस्तुत करते हैं बिना गवाह-कटघरे में खींचे जाने और प्रति-परीक्षित होने की इच्छा के।

sections.title: Witnesses to character
sections.raw_text: Witnesses to character may be cross-examined and re-examined.

breakdown.plain_summary: Character witnesses are not exempt from the ordinary examination process — they too can be cross-examined and re-examined like any other witness.
essential_elements: Character witnesses are subject to cross-examination and re-examination.
breakdown.how_to_read: A short confirmatory section — removes any doubt that character evidence gets special protection from normal testing.

sections.title: Leading questions
sections.raw_text:
(1) Any question suggesting the answer which the person putting it wishes or expects to receive, is called a leading question.

(2) Leading questions must not, if objected to by the adverse party, be asked in an examination-in-chief, or in a re-examination, except with the permission of the Court.

(3) The Court shall permit leading questions as to matters which are introductory or undisputed, or which have, in its opinion, been already sufficiently proved.

(4) Leading questions may be asked in cross-examination.

breakdown.plain_summary: Defines leading questions and where they're allowed: generally barred (if objected to) in examination-in-chief and re-examination, but permitted for introductory/undisputed/already-proved matters, and freely permitted in cross-examination.
essential_elements: Leading question = one that suggests the desired answer.
Barred in chief/re-examination only if objected to by the adverse party — not an automatic bar.
Court must permit leading questions for introductory, undisputed, or already-sufficiently-proved matters.
Freely permitted in cross-examination (no restriction).
exceptions_and_qualifications: The bar in chief/re-examination is objection-triggered, not automatic — if the adverse party doesn't object, a leading question can stand.
breakdown.how_to_read: Classic trial-advocacy rule: no leading your own witness on contested matters (unless unopposed or the Court allows it for uncontested ground), but leading is the norm in cross-examination.

sections.title: Evidence as to matters in writing
sections.raw_text:
Any witness may be asked, while under examination, whether any contract, grant or other disposition of property, as to which he is giving evidence, was not contained in a document, and if he says that it was, or if he is about to make any statement as to the contents of any document, which, in the opinion of the Court, ought to be produced, the adverse party may object to such evidence being given until such document is produced, or until facts have been proved which entitle the party who called the witness to give secondary evidence of it.

Explanation.—A witness may give oral evidence of statements made by other persons about the contents of documents if such statements are in themselves relevant facts.

Illustration
The question is, whether A assaulted B. C deposes that he heard A say to D—"B wrote a letter accusing me of theft, and I will be revenged on him". This statement is relevant, as showing A's motive for the assault, and evidence may be given of it, though no other evidence is given about the letter.

breakdown.plain_summary: Enforces the documents-over-oral-testimony preference at the examination stage: if a witness's evidence effectively restates a document's contents, the adverse party can demand the document be produced (or secondary evidence conditions be met) before that oral evidence continues. But testimony about statements that are independently relevant (e.g. as showing motive) is not caught by this bar, even if those statements refer to a document's existence.
essential_elements: Applies where a witness's evidence concerns a contract/grant/disposition that was reduced to a document.
Adverse party may object and demand production of the document (or proof enabling secondary evidence) before the oral account continues.

Explanation carve-out: oral evidence of a third party's statement about a document's contents is fine if the statement itself is independently relevant (not being used to prove the document's contents).
exceptions_and_qualifications: The illustration is key: the letter's contents are never proved, but the fact that A referenced the letter and threatened revenge is independently relevant to show motive — that's different from trying to prove what the letter said.
breakdown.how_to_read: Link back to the best-evidence-rule ss.94-95 (Chapter VI) — s.147 is the trial-mechanics enforcement tool for that same document-priority principle.

sections.title: Cross-examination as to previous statements in writing
sections.raw_text: A witness may be cross-examined as to previous statements made by him in writing or reduced into writing, and relevant to matters in question, without such writing being shown to him, or being proved; but, if it is intended to contradict him by the writing, his attention must, before the writing can be proved, be called to those parts of it which are to be used for the purpose of contradicting him.

breakdown.plain_summary: A witness can be cross-examined about their own earlier written statements without first showing them the writing — but if counsel actually wants to use that writing to contradict them (impeach credibility), the witness's attention must first be drawn to the specific contradicting portions before the writing is formally proved.
essential_elements: Cross-examination on prior written statements is allowed without first showing or proving the writing.
To use the writing to contradict the witness, the specific contradicting parts must first be put to the witness before the writing is proved.
breakdown.how_to_read: This is the procedural foundation for classic impeachment-by-prior-statement cross-examination — fairness requires giving the witness a chance to explain before the document is formally proved against them.

sections.title: Questions lawful in cross-examination
sections.raw_text:
When a witness is cross-examined, he may, in addition to the questions hereinbefore referred to, be asked any questions which tend—
(a) to test his veracity; or
(b) to discover who he is and what is his position in life; or
(c) to shake his credit, by injuring his character, although the answer to such questions might tend directly or indirectly to criminate him, or might expose or tend directly or indirectly to expose him to a penalty or forfeiture:

Provided that in a prosecution for an offence under section 64, section 65, section 66, section 67, section 68, section 69, section 70 or section 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or for attempt to commit any such offence, where the question of consent is an issue, it shall not be permissible to adduce evidence or to put questions in the cross-examination of the victim as to the general immoral character, or previous sexual experience, of such victim with any person for proving such consent or the quality of consent.

breakdown.plain_summary: Broadens permissible cross-examination to include credibility-testing, identity, and character-attacking questions, even where answers might self-incriminate. But the proviso carves out a crucial protection: in sexual offence prosecutions where consent is in issue, the victim cannot be cross-examined on general immoral character or past sexual history to prove consent.
essential_elements: Permissible cross-examination purposes: testing veracity, establishing identity/position in life, and shaking credit via character.
Such questions are allowed even if the answer could tend to incriminate the witness or expose them to penalty/forfeiture.
Proviso bars questioning a sexual-offence victim's general immoral character or prior sexual history to prove consent, in prosecutions under BNS ss.64-71 (and attempts thereof).
exceptions_and_qualifications: The proviso is a significant victim-protection reform — it forecloses the old 'character assassination' cross-examination tactic in rape/sexual-assault trials on the consent question.
breakdown.how_to_read: Flag the proviso prominently in any sexual-offence trial prep — it is a hard bar, not a discretionary one, on a specific and historically abused line of cross-examination.

sections.title: When witness to be compelled to answer
sections.raw_text: If any such question relates to a matter relevant to the suit or proceeding, the provisions of section 137 shall apply thereto.

breakdown.plain_summary: Where a s.149-type character/credit question also happens to be relevant to the case itself (not just to credit), the s.137 rule kicks in — the witness must answer despite self-incrimination concerns, but gets use immunity for the compelled answer.
essential_elements: Applies only where the s.149 question is also relevant to the matter in issue.
In that overlap, s.137 (compelled answer + use immunity) governs.
breakdown.how_to_read: A cross-referencing bridge section — it routes relevance-overlapping credit questions back into the s.137 compulsion-plus-immunity framework.

sections.title: Court to decide when question shall be asked and when witness compelled to answer

breakdown.plain_summary: For purely credit-damaging questions with no independent relevance, the Court has discretion whether to compel an answer, guided by four factors: seriousness of impact on credibility, remoteness/triviality of the imputation, proportionality between the character attack and the importance of the evidence, and the option to draw an adverse inference from refusal.
essential_elements: Applies to questions relevant only to credit, not to the substance of the case.
Court has discretion to compel or excuse the answer, and may warn the witness they need not answer.

Four guiding considerations: seriousness of the imputation's effect on credibility; remoteness/triviality cutting against compulsion; disproportionality between the attack and the evidence's importance cutting against compulsion; and permissible adverse inference from refusal.
breakdown.how_to_read: This is the discretionary balancing counterpart to s.149's broader permission — s.149 says such questions CAN be asked, s.151 tells the Court how to decide whether the witness must actually answer.

sections.title: Question not to be asked without reasonable grounds
sections.raw_text:
No such question as is referred to in section 151 ought to be asked, unless the person asking it has reasonable grounds for thinking that the imputation which it conveys is well-founded.

Illustrations
(a) An advocate is instructed by another advocate that an important witness is a dacoit. This is a reasonable ground for asking the witness whether he is a dacoit.
(b) An advocate is informed by a person in Court that an important witness is a dacoit. The informant, on being questioned by the advocate, gives satisfactory reasons for his statement. This is a reasonable ground for asking the witness whether he is a dacoit.
(c) A witness, of whom nothing whatever is known, is asked at random whether he is a dacoit. There are here no reasonable grounds for the question.
(d) A witness, of whom nothing whatever is known, being questioned as to his mode of life and means of living, gives unsatisfactory answers. This may be a reasonable ground for asking him if he is a dacoit.

breakdown.plain_summary: Imposes a good-faith requirement on s.151-type credit-attacking questions: counsel must have reasonable grounds to believe the imputation is true before asking, illustrated by contrasts between properly-instructed questions and random fishing expeditions.
essential_elements: Reasonable grounds for believing the imputation well-founded are a precondition to asking a s.151 question.

Illustrations distinguish instructed/corroborated grounds (proper) from asking 'at random' with no information (improper), and note that unsatisfactory answers during questioning can themselves generate reasonable grounds.
breakdown.how_to_read: Pair with s.153: this section sets the good-faith precondition, s.153 supplies the sanction (report to the High Court/disciplinary authority) for advocates who breach it.

sections.title: Procedure of Court in case of question being asked without reasonable grounds
sections.raw_text: If the Court is of opinion that any such question was asked without reasonable grounds, it may, if it was asked by any advocate, report the circumstances of the case to the High Court or other authority to which such advocate is subject in the exercise of his profession.

breakdown.plain_summary: Provides the enforcement mechanism for s.152: an advocate who asks a baseless character-attacking question can be reported by the Court to the High Court or the relevant disciplinary authority.
essential_elements: Applies where the Court finds a s.151/152 question was asked without reasonable grounds.
Sanction: the Court may report the advocate to the High Court or other disciplinary authority.
breakdown.how_to_read: The disciplinary backstop that gives s.152's good-faith requirement real teeth against abusive cross-examination tactics.

sections.title: Indecent and scandalous questions
sections.raw_text: The Court may forbid any questions or inquiries which it regards as indecent or scandalous, although such questions or inquiries may have some bearing on the questions before the Court, unless they relate to facts in issue, or to matters necessary to be known in order to determine whether or not the facts in issue existed.

breakdown.plain_summary: Gives the Court a general power to block indecent or scandalous questions even if somewhat relevant, unless they concern facts actually in issue or facts necessary to determine those issues.
essential_elements: Court may forbid indecent/scandalous questions notwithstanding some relevance.
Exception: questions relating to facts in issue, or facts necessary to determine whether those facts in issue existed, cannot be forbidden on this ground.
breakdown.how_to_read: A general decorum/dignity-protecting power for the Court, cabined so it cannot be used to suppress genuinely necessary evidence on the actual issues in the case.

sections.title: Questions intended to insult or annoy
sections.raw_text: The Court shall forbid any question which appears to it to be intended to insult or annoy, or which, though proper in itself, appears to the Court needlessly offensive in form.

breakdown.plain_summary: Even a technically proper question must be forbidden by the Court if it is designed to insult or annoy the witness, or is phrased in a needlessly offensive way — a mandatory (not discretionary) duty on the Court, unlike s.154's 'may forbid'.
essential_elements: Court must (mandatory 'shall') forbid questions intended to insult or annoy.
